stops.name: Milan, Il Fuoco published, the love betrayed in print
stops.campa: In March 1900 Treves of Milan issues Il Fuoco, and Europe reads, barely veiled, the anatomy of his nights with Duse: Foscarina, the great actress aging, studied like a specimen by the young orator who loves and uses her. The scandal is continental; friends beg her to stop the book. She refuses: her suffering, she says, does not count when another masterpiece is to be given to Italian literature. It is the most complete sentence of love and the most complete betrayal in the canon, and both are true.

stops.name: Rome, Montecitorio, the walk toward life
stops.campa: In the chamber, during the debates on the laws of public safety, the deputy of Beauty rises from the benches of the Right, crosses the floor before the whole parliament, and sits with the Extreme Left, saying that as a man of intellect he goes toward life. The gesture is pure theatre and pure omen: he belongs to no party but motion itself. In the next elections the seat is lost and never missed. Parliaments, he has learned, are rooms; he requires balconies.
stops.quote: Come uomo d'intelletto, vado verso la vita.
stops.quote_source: Declaration in the Chamber of Deputies, March 1900

stops.name: Rome, Teatro Costanzi, Francesca da Rimini with Duse
stops.campa: On 9 December 1901, at the Costanzi, Eleonora Duse is Francesca in the tragedy he has built for her out of Dante's fifth canto: a Malatesta Rimini reconstructed arch by arch, armourers' invoices and all, the most expensive staging Italy has seen. The poem of the kiss over the book, given back to the theatre six centuries later. The public quarrels, the box office triumphs, and the pair stand at the summit of their joined arts, exactly at the moment the descent is prepared.

stops.name: Marina di Pisa, the pine wood of the rain
stops.campa: The Alcyone summer: with Eleonora at Marina di Pisa, between the Arno mouth and the Tombolo pines, the Tuscan July and August of 1902 turn directly into verse. Rain comes over the pineta and the two lovers walking in it are changed into vegetable creatures, faces dripping green: La pioggia nel pineto is written as weather. Ermione walks here forever. The greatest Italian lyric sequence of the century is a holiday diary; the canon holds that for one season a man transcribed the Mediterranean itself.
stops.quote: Taci. Su le soglie del bosco non odo parole che dici umane; ma odo parole più nuove che parlano gocciole e foglie lontane.

stops.name: Milan, Teatro Lirico, La figlia di Iorio without Duse
stops.campa: On 2 March 1904 the Teatro Lirico gives La figlia di Iorio, the pastoral tragedy of the Abruzzo: Mila di Codra hunted by reapers, the ancient shepherd world made liturgy. It is his greatest theatrical triumph, and Eleonora Duse is not on the stage: ill at Genoa, she is replaced by Irma Gramatica, and the role written in her blood is given away. The wound is final. The love of the age ends not with a scene but with a casting decision; Duse and the poet do not meet again for twenty years.

stops.name: Montichiari, the Brescia air circuit, the poet takes wing
stops.campa: At the Brescia air meeting of September 1909, on the plain of Montichiari, he climbs behind Glenn Curtiss and leaves the earth for the first time. Kafka is in the crowd, taking notes on the small stern-faced Italian celebrity. The flight lasts minutes; the conversion lasts the rest of his life. Icarus enters the Laudi; the novel Forse che sì forse che no gives Italy its first aviator hero. He has found the machine adequate to his myth, and he already knows there is a war coming that will require it.

stops.name: Settignano, the creditors take the Capponcina
stops.campa: The arithmetic arrives at last. In March 1910, hounded by a mountain of protested bills, he leaves the Capponcina by night: the greyhounds, the casts, the damasks, the four thousand books all abandoned to the bailiffs, who will auction the whole reliquary piece by piece the following year. He does not watch. Ruin is reframed as departure: the ship for France is called exile, and exile is called a Latin poet's right. The villa empties; the legend, unencumbered, travels light.

stops.name: Paris, the exile arrives and is crowned
stops.campa: Paris receives the fugitive as a reigning prince of letters: Montesquiou presents him, the salons dispute him, Ida Rubinstein and the Ballets Russes orbit near. He arrives owing everything and within a month is dining as the guest of honour of the Republic of taste. He writes now in French as well, to the scandal and admiration of the Académie's antechambers. The exile is golden by his own decree: Italy, he lets it be known, is not lost but merely waiting for him to be necessary.

stops.name: Arcachon, the Villa Saint-Dominique among the dunes
stops.campa: At Le Moulleau by Arcachon he takes the Villa Saint-Dominique, pines and ocean and the great dune southward: an Atlantic Landes to replace the lost Tuscan hill. Greyhounds again, horses again, debts again, and the work pouring out: French dramas, the martyrology, the odes. Nathalie de Goloubeff, the amazon of the kennels, keeps his hounds and his heart's ledger. He rides the empty beaches in winter and calls the fog of Gascony a good workshop for an Italian who is preparing thunder.

stops.name: Paris, Théâtre du Châtelet, Le Martyre de Saint Sébastien
stops.campa: On 22 May 1911 the Châtelet gives Le Martyre de Saint Sébastien: his French verse mystery, Debussy's music, Bakst's décor, Ida Rubinstein's androgynous saint pierced by arrows. A week before the opening the Archbishop of Paris forbids Catholics to attend, and Rome places the poet's works on the Index: the martyrdom is thus performed twice, once on stage and once upon the author, exactly as he would have written it. Debussy and the Jew Rubinstein and the pagan d'Annunzio, censured together, take their bows.

stops.name: Arcachon, the Canzoni della gesta d'oltremare
stops.campa: When Italy goes to Libya, the exile's desk becomes a battery. From Arcachon he fires the Canzoni della gesta d'oltremare into the Corriere della Sera: the songs of the overseas deed, Dante's metres retooled for dreadnoughts and desert columns. One canzone insults Austria so directly that the censor blanks it out, and the blank page is read more avidly than any verses. From the Atlantic dunes he has resumed command of Italian patriotism by post. The nation notices that its war poet lives abroad, and is ashamed.

stops.name: Paris, the summons: Quarto calls the exile home
stops.campa: Spring 1915: Italy hangs between neutrality and the war, and the letter comes to Paris: the invitation to speak at Quarto, where Garibaldi's Thousand embarked, at the unveiling of their monument. He recognizes the shape of the hour instantly: a nation requiring a voice, a shore requiring a prophet, five years of exile requiring an ending. He drafts the oration in the French capital while the French armies hold the Marne. The debts remain in France; the man is repatriated by destiny, first class.
